questions.question: Why was Elizabeth's education unusual for a woman of her time? (2 marks)

points.text: Elizabeth's education was unusual because she received a humanist education normally reserved for boys: she was tutored by leading scholars like Roger Ascham, became fluent in Latin, Greek, French, Italian, and Spanish, studied rhetoric, philosophy, and theology, and was skilled in music. Most women of the era received only basic domestic education.

questions.question: Describe two challenges Elizabeth faced when she became queen in November 1558. (4 marks)

points.text: Two challenges: (1) Religious division - England had swung from Henry VIII's break with Rome to Edward VI's Protestantism to Mary I's Catholic restoration, leaving the country deeply divided; (2) Financial crisis - Mary I left the Crown approximately £300,000 in debt. Other challenges include war with France, loss of Calais, and questions about Elizabeth's legitimacy.

questions.question: Explain why Elizabeth called her Religious Settlement a "middle way." (4 marks)

points.text: The Settlement was a "middle way" because it was designed to be a compromise between Catholicism and Protestantism. questions.question: Explain the significance of the 1570 papal excommunication of Elizabeth. (4 marks)

points.text: The 1570 excommunication was significant because it transformed Catholicism from a religious difference into a political threat. By absolving Catholics of their allegiance to Elizabeth, Pope Pius V made being Catholic equivalent to being a potential traitor.
